messages:
rachel_finance: Quick follow-up from today's AH finance segment — can we get a concrete definition of 'constrain discretionary spend' for procurement planning?
sam_ceo: Short answer: prioritize customer-impacting, compliance, revenue-driving work. Delay non-essential infra experiments and big new vendor bets this quarter. :white_check_mark:
maria_fp&a: Baseline planning assumption = 18 months runway. If a team wants to plan to 12 months, escalate to FP&A with a clear tradeoff memo.
finance-bot: [automated] Procurement thresholds reminder: < $10k = manager; $10k–$75k = manager + finance; > $75k = exec + legal.
jordan_eng: Clarify: do multi-month reserved infra commits (Dedicated GPU pools) count towards the $75k threshold?
maria_fp&a: Yes. Multi-month or multi-year commitments count as contract value. If it pushes you over $75k, do a pre-review with FP&A before procurement.
rachel_finance: Is there an expedited path for security/compliance spending (pen tests, SOC2, certs)? Some deadlines are tight.
nina_ops: Yes — security/compliance requests have a fast-track checkbox. Ping @nina_ops and include a short impact statement; I will triage within 48 hours.
sam_ceo: Also loop procurement in early for vendor talks. We have negotiation templates that often add credits or shorten payback windows.
rachel_finance: For hiring: should managers freeze new IC headcount or only backfills?
sam_ceo: Backfills for revenue, reliability, or customer-facing roles are approved. New headcount or role expansion needs a secondary FP&A review. Keep hiring conservative. :chart_with_downwards_trend:
maria_fp&a: Action: teams submit a 1-paragraph justification for active procurements and open hires by EOD next Friday. Priority to items with direct ROI or compliance rationale.
jordan_eng: Can FP&A share a one-page checklist so reviews are faster?
maria_fp&a: Yes — I will post a template in procurement docs and tag managers.
rachel_finance: Guidance on vendor pre-pay discounts?
sam_ceo: Include 6/12/18 month scenarios in the request showing impact on monthly burn. If pre-pay materially improves unit economics, include the plan; otherwise prefer shorter commitments.
nina_ops: Ops will run a quick burn-impact calc for any pre-pay > $25k.
finance-bot: [automated] Procurement docs: https://confluence.redwood.example/procurement-guidelines
rachel_finance: One last thing — fast lane for urgent infra renewals that would affect SLAs?
maria_fp&a: Tag requests "URGENT-SLA" with customer impact. FP&A + Ops will aim for a 48h turnaround on those.
rachel_finance: Thanks all, I will collate questions and share the 1-paragraph template once Maria posts it. :thumbsup:
